title: Çin'de yerli elektronik mimariye sahip ilk insansı robot tanıtıldı
summary: Çin, yapay zeka kararları ile fiziksel hareketleri tamamen yerli elektronik mimariyle birleştiren dünyanın ilk insansı robotunu tanıttı.
body:
Çin'in Hubei eyaletinin Yichang şehrinde, tamamen yerli olarak geliştirilen elektronik bir mimariye sahip dünyanın ilk yapay zeka destekli insansı robotu görücüye çıktı. CCTV News'in aktardığına göre, bu yeni sistem robotun yapay zeka kararlarını fiziksel eylemlere dönüştüren kritik katmanda dışa bağımlılığa karşı yerli bir alternatif sunuyor.

## Güvenlik testleri ve mimari yapı

Elektronik mimari; işletim sistemini, ağları, yazılım araçlarını, bilgi işlem çiplerini ve kontrol işlevlerini bir araya getiriyor. Shanghai University for Science and Technology bünyesindeki Machine Intelligence Enstitüsü'nden Li Qingdu, Global Times'a yaptığı açıklamada, yapay zekanın düşündüğü ile robotun yaptığı arasında güvenli ve kontrol edilebilir bir altyapı gerektiğini belirtti. Geliştiriciler, test personelinin robotu eklem hasarı, siber saldırı ve virüs bulaştırma gibi zorlu koşullar altında değerlendirdiğini bildirdi. Aktarılan bilgilere göre yeni robot bu testler sırasında güvenli çalışmaya devam etti.

## Yerli kontrol hedefi

Bu gelişme, Çin'in robotik endüstrisinde yalnızca bireysel parçaları yerlileştirmekle kalmayıp bunları birbirine bağlayan temel mimariyi de kontrol altına alma çabasının bir parçasını oluşturuyor. Ülkenin Sanayi ve Bilgi Teknolojileri Bakanlığı 2023 yılında güvenli bir sanayi ve tedarik zinciri sistemi çağrısında bulunmuştu, ayrıca 2026-2030 yıllarını kapsayan 15. Beş Yıllık Plan taslağında da robotik endüstrisi öncelikli alanlar arasında yer alıyor.

**Neden önemli?** Geliştirilen bu yerli elektronik mimari, Çin'in robotik sektöründe dışa bağımlılığı azaltma ve kritik altyapılarda özerklik kazanma stratejisinde önemli bir adım olarak öne çıkıyor.

topic: China unveils world's first humanoid built around domestic electronic architecture

source_texts.title: China unveils world’s first humanoid built around a domestic electronic architecture
source_texts.summary: China has unveiled what it describes as the world’s first embodied AI robot equipped with...
source_texts.text:
China has unveiled what it describes as the world’s first embodied AI robot equipped with a fully domestically developed electronic architecture. The robot was presented Monday in Yichang, Hubei Province, according to CCTV News.
The architecture connects the robot’s AI decision-making with its physical actions. Its developers say the system offers a domestic alternative to foreign technologies used in this critical layer of robotics.
The unveiling comes as China seeks greater control over the systems beneath its growing robotics industry. Developers also reported that the robot maintained safe operation during tests involving damaged joints, cyberattacks and implanted viruses.
The system between thought and movement
An electronic architecture brings together a robot’s operating system, networking, software tools, computing chips and control functions. It determines how decisions made by AI are translated into instructions that the machine can carry out.
The developers say their architecture allows control functions and AI computing to operate separately while remaining integrated. They describe it as a domestic foundation extending from AI decision-making to physical execution.
“What AI ‘thinks’ is one thing, and what a robot ‘does’ is another. In between, there must be a reliable, secure and controllable underlying system. The electronic architecture is that system,” Li Qingdu, executive dean of the Institute of Machine Intelligence at the University of Shanghai for Science and Technology, told the Global Times.
Li said the development reflects a broader shift in China’s robotics industry: from making individual components domestically to developing the underlying architecture that connects them. The announcement did not identify the robot’s manufacturer or provide detailed technical specifications.
Safety under simulated failures
Testing personnel evaluated the robot under conditions that included joint damage, cyberattacks, and virus implantation, according to the report. It said robots using conventional electronic architectures suffered circuit failures, sudden shutdowns or loss of control under those conditions.
The new robot reportedly continued operating safely. The reported results point to the architecture’s ability to respond quickly, isolate faults, and protect the system when something goes wrong, though the account did not provide test methods or independent verification.
Those capabilities matter when robots work near people. Li pointed to concerns raised at robot competitions about possible collisions, arguing that the underlying system must keep a robot within physical and operational safety limits even when it encounters a fault or attack.
A broader push for domestic control
The robot’s electronic architecture is part of China’s effort to build more of its robotics technology at home. According to the developers, it provides an option that could replace foreign solutions for the systems connecting AI computing and machine control.
“Localization here is not simply about replacing suppliers across the industrial chain. It is also about gaining autonomous control over the underlying systems of robots,” Li said.
China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology called for a secure and reliable industrial and supply chain system by 2027 in a guideline released in 2023.
A draft outline of the country’s 15th Five-Year Plan, covering 2026 to 2030, also identifies robotics as an emerging industry for accelerated development.
